text.p: Shares in Belgian construction company Moury Construct began trading on the main, continuous forward market of the Brussels bourse on Friday at 3,070 Belgian francs with an initial volume of 716 shares traded.
The company stems from the absorption of Moury and Bemat by Solinvest in November 1996, with the whole restructured group renamed Moury Construct and lined up for a single listing.
Forty percent, or 401,952 ordinary shares, of its capital are now listed on the bourse. The remaining shares are held by the Moury family.
The group recently completed a restructuring aimed at simplifying its structure and making its shares more attractive.
Moury Construct's 1995 operating income was 1.8 billion francs, lead manager Bank Degroof said. It forecast operating income to rise to 1.95 billion francs for 1996.
The bank said operating margins attained 8.1 percent over the past three years compared to a sector average of 2.5 percent.
Moury specialises in the construction of industrial and office buildings, public buildings and renovation. In the residential sector it builds publicly-funded social housing.
